summary: OAI 142 (deterministic factoring over F_p) is assessed in OAI_METHOD_142.md; ES search uses square roots mod p only through the deterministic path already discussed there.

The threshold 4C ≥ (4Cp+1)^{1/4} is equivalent to C ≳ p^{1/3}/4 (checked by hand). The Coppersmith bivariate regime for exactly this modulus is already worked out in ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO.md, pass-1 entry for Z1766 (line ~263: W ≈ p at the certificate scale, u ≳ p^{1/3}/4). The factor-finding framing adds nothing new.

Lit check: erdosproblems.com/298 (Bloom 2021): yes, with positive upper density, for sums of distinct reciprocals. This is a density statement for subsets; ES needs every prime p, so no uniform lower bound follows.
Vague: 'quantify the number of independent parameters vs constraints' names no computation or object.
variants2.json already has the claim. I re-verified for n <= 1000: failures of 'some solution with 4 not dividing xyz' are exactly the multiples of 16 (62 values, no exceptions either way).

Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture (quaternion proof for integral solutions) is already analysed in the repo: BRAINSTORM/z52b_pass1_L00.md (Z0394) reads Machiavelo–Tsopanidis arXiv:2003.02592; the 'four-square-like refinements' are the same family, so the 200-predicate search is a new generator, not a new mechanism.
Generic: 'choose a small discriminant' with no ES congruence named.
Sylvester-wave derivation for R(p) as a double sum: analytic derivation only, no numerical test defined.
Same source as Z2114 (arXiv 2504.10992): the audit of local tests needs the full paper, which was not read. From the abstract, the failing mechanism is BM, which Bright–Loughran say is absent for ES.

Partial Spearman of residual log U with tau(p-1), controlling for L(1,chi_p) (computed via the Dirichlet L-formula), p=1 mod 4 below 6000 (n=372): -0.22 (raw -0.56). tau(p-1) stays significant, so L(1,chi_p) does not absorb it.
Pure restatement: 4L/p = L/x+L/y+L/z is the ES identity multiplied by L.

Checked the claim that an ES certificate condition is a 'difference set avoids P(primes)' statement. The ES conditions are divisibility conditions on 4Cp+1 and are not expressed as a difference set of polynomial values, so the OAI-182 power-saving statement does not apply as stated.

Same enumeration, all odd primes ≤1500: min(y−x)=0 first occurs at p=7, and 51% of primes have a solution with y−x≤2. The p≡1 (mod 4) restriction in the item was not split out, so this is a partial answer.
